data.text: @averycode This hits. Started coding at 49 with zero background, building at 9 PM after the kids are down. Just shipped my first iOS app, still keeping the day job. The compounding is real, you just can't see it from inside month one.

Google just shipped AI Edge Eloquent — a free dictation app that removes filler words in real time, runs entirely offline, and it's already on iOS.

No internet needed. Your voice data never leaves the device.

Here's why this matters more than another transcription tool:

Most dictation apps transcribe everything — every "um", "uh", mid-sentence correction, restart. You get raw speech as text, which still needs editing. AI Edge Eloquent flips this: it captures what you MEANT to say, not what you actually said.

The offline engine uses Google's Gemma architecture on-device. Enable online mode and it taps Gemini for deeper cleanup, smart rewrites, and key-point extraction.

You can import your Gmail contacts and jargon via Dictionaries tab — names, niche terms, industry acronyms. Accuracy improves over time as it learns your vocabulary.

Output options:
- Polish → clean, readable text
- Key Points → summary (online only)
- Formal / Short / Long rewrites

Plus WPM stats and word count — useful for anyone tracking speaking clarity.

Why I'm watching this: Google is quietly building the on-device AI stack. Gemma → AI Edge → now Eloquent. The same pattern as Pixel's on-device AI features — but this time it's a standalone iOS app, not tied to any hardware.

If it comes to Android, it replaces Wispr Flow, MacWhisper, and SuperWhisper for anyone who values privacy over cloud features.

Free, no account required, works offline. That's a rare combination.

Cursor just shipped a native iOS app — and it's more than a remote desktop.

You can launch cloud agents from your phone, control agents running on your computer remotely, and get push notifications when work is ready. Voice input, slash commands, full model selection.

The workflows that work today:
- Incident on-call → kick off an agent from lunch, come back to a PR
- Customer bug report → start a fix from your phone while away from desk

Cloud agents run in isolated VMs with full dev environments. They produce demos, screenshots, and logs. You can review diffs, leave follow-up instructions, or merge the PR directly from the app.

The handoff between local and cloud is the interesting part. Send a local plan to a cloud agent, or move an active cloud session back to your machine for local testing before merging.

This is the most serious mobile coding agent I've seen. Not a companion app — a full agent platform in your pocket.

We’re currently hard at work improving the response quality of our agentic swarm on the private edition Mac app for VeriRFP, using on-device AI while also pushing response speed. On the side I’ve been building something that came straight out of frustration at home.
My wife and daughter constantly complain about how exhausting social media has become. The endless rage bait, doomscrolling, and algorithms that seem designed to keep everyone angry and scrolling. It got me thinking there has to be a better way for adults to actually connect with people nearby.
That’s why I started MetroMeet. An 18+ social app built for real, low-pressure connections in your own area. The tagline says it best: “Meet people, not arguments.”
It’s a modern take on the fun, local, playful social apps a lot of us remember from earlier days of the internet. Your area’s wall where people post plans, questions, and everyday thoughts. Real verified profiles with personality. Simple games and icebreakers so conversations actually start. Optional private filters for compatibility — including partisanship if you want — so you can choose who sees you and who you interact with. You earn MetroBucks just by showing up and being decent, and you can spend them on virtual gifts or other playful stuff.
We launch city by city once enough locals join the waitlist. That way every area starts with real density and energy instead of a ghost town. No video feeds. No influencers. No algorithms pushing outrage. Just relationship-first connection over endless scrolling.
I just shipped the waitlist site yesterday at https://t.co/uwawqQSEig. If this resonates, claim your founding spot. Early members get priority access when their area launches, a founding badge, starting MetroBucks, and referral boosts.
We’re moving fast on the iOS side too and would love your thoughts.
What do you miss most about the earlier, lighter days of social apps, or what would actually make one enjoyable again for adults?

Google just shipped a dictation app that runs entirely on-device — no internet required, no audio leaves your phone.

Google AI Edge Eloquent is free on iOS and does something most transcription tools don't: it strips filler words ("um," "uh") in real time and smooths your phrasing before you see the text.

The offline mode runs on Google's Gemma architecture directly on your device. Connect your Gmail to import custom names and jargon. The Dictionaries tab lets you add niche terms manually.

Online features tap Gemini for deeper cleanup, summaries, and rewrite styles (formal, short, long). But the base experience works without any network.

Why this is interesting:
- Privacy-first: voice data never leaves the device
- Real-time filler word removal — not post-processing
- Speaking speed stats (WPM) + word count for communication improvement
- Free, with no subscription

The big question: will this come to Android? Right now it's iOS-only. If Google brings the same on-device Gemma stack to Android, this becomes a genuinely useful cross-platform tool.

https://t.co/YSY0y4yXqz

Cursor just shipped a native iOS app — and it changes how I think about AI coding agents.

The core insight is simple: inspiration doesn't always happen at a desk. The Cursor iOS app lets you start agents, review diffs, and merge PRs from your phone. Voice input, slash commands, push notifications when agents finish.

But the architecture is what's interesting. The app connects to agents running either locally or in Cursor's cloud VMs. You can start a task locally, shift it to the cloud mid-task, and pull it back to your machine to test before merging. The mobile app is the control layer in the middle.

Real-world workflows they highlight:
- On-call incidents: get paged at lunch → launch an agent from your phone → a PR is waiting when you get back
- Customer bugs: reproduce and fix while away from your desk
- Design feedback: screenshot X/Twitter feedback → annotate → send as visual context to an agent

Cloud agents run in isolated VMs with full dev environments. They produce demos, screenshots, and logs. Push notifications and Live Activities keep you updated without staying in the app.

This is the shift: AI coding assistants are moving from desktop tools to always-on infrastructure. Agents that run in the background, report back when ready, and don't need a developer staring at a screen.

Available on all paid plans. 75% off Composer 2.5 runs through July 5.

🚨BREAKING: Apple has blocked agentic AI from the App Store for years.

this week, one finally got through.

OpenClaw just launched native iOS and Android apps.

the reason Apple approved it is in the privacy label.

WHAT JUST HAPPENED:

OpenClaw dropped native mobile apps for iOS and Android.

the launch thread pulled 1.5 million views within hours.

the App Store listing reads: "Data Not Collected."

that line is why it cleared review.

nothing routes through a company server.

your data and automations live on your own gateway.

Apple had no data practices to object to.

HOW IT WORKS:

the phone does not run the AI.

it pairs with your self-hosted OpenClaw Gateway running on a Mac, Linux box, or Windows machine.

scan a QR code. your phone becomes a node in your personal agent network.

→ chat with your agent or switch to real-time Talk mode
→ approve or deny every action the agent wants to take
→ grant optional access to camera, location, photos, contacts, calendar
→ on android: "hey google, ask OpenClaw" routes straight into the app

your agent lives on your hardware.

your phone is the remote.

THE NUMBERS:

→ 247k GitHub stars in under three months
→ 1.17 million weekly npm downloads
→ 5,400+ installable skill packs
→ 20+ connected channels: telegram, whatsapp, signal, slack, discord, imessage

THE CATCH:

→ not a standalone app. no gateway, no agent
→ setup requires a terminal. this is still an operator tool
→ early android reviews are rough. crashes and pairing issues reported
→ prompt injection warnings still apply. approvals matter

THE BIGGER PICTURE:

every AI company is racing to put an assistant in your pocket.

OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic are all shipping cloud agents.

OpenClaw just shipped the opposite.

the agent stays on your machine.

the cloud never sees your data.

and Apple, the most privacy-obsessed gatekeeper in tech, let it through the wall first.

google is reportedly building a 24/7 personal agent to compete with it directly.

it’s as if the open source project is moving faster than the trillion dollar companies.

the phone in your pocket just became a control surface for an agent you own.

not rent.

own.
